1.modern-en: Seven-year-old Sara arrives in London from India with her father and is installed at Miss Minchin's seminary as a pampered parlor boarder. She notices from the start that Miss Minchin tells flattering lies, and confides to her father that she finds the school rather like going into battle. When he leaves, she locks herself in her room and sits silently on the floor beside Emily rather than crying.
1.modern-da: Den syvårige Sara ankommer til London fra Indien med sin far og indkvarteres på Miss Minchins pensionat som en priviligeret pensionist. Allerede fra starten bemærker hun, at Miss Minchin siger smiger-løgne, og betror sin far, at skolen minder hende om at gå i krig. Da han tager afsted, låser hun sig inde på sit værelse og sidder stille på gulvet ved siden af Emily i stedet for at græde.

2.modern-en: On her first morning in the schoolroom, Sara discovers she is expected to learn beginner French — a language she already speaks fluently from childhood. She tries politely to explain this, but Miss Minchin silences her; it is only when Monsieur Dufarge arrives and hears her speak that the truth comes out. From that moment, Miss Minchin begins to resent her.
2.modern-da: På sin første morgen i skolestuen opdager Sara, at hun forventes at lære begynder-fransk — et sprog, hun allerede taler flydende fra barndommen. Hun forsøger høfligt at forklare dette, men Miss Minchin tier hende ihjel; det er først da Monsieur Dufarge ankommer og hører hende tale, at sandheden kommer frem. Fra det øjeblik begynder Miss Minchin at nære et had til hende.

3.modern-en: Sara befriends the slow, tearful Ermengarde St. John after class, invites her upstairs to meet Emily, and tells her stories. When Ermengarde asks if Sara loves her father, Sara says quietly: "I love mine more than all the world ten times over. That is what my pain is. He has gone away." She promises to help Ermengarde with French lessons.
3.modern-da: Sara bliver venner med den langsomme, grådkvalte Ermengarde St. John efter time, inviterer hende op for at møde Emily og fortæller hende historier. Da Ermengarde spørger, om Sara elsker sin far, siger Sara stille: »Jeg elsker min mere end hele verden ti gange om. Det er min smerte. Han er rejst bort.« Hun lover at hjælpe Ermengarde med fransklektion.

4.modern-en: Sara reflects that her comfortable life has never truly tested her character — she wonders if she might secretly be a horrid child. She quiets the screaming Lottie by sitting down beside her on the floor and admitting she also has no mother, then invents a story about heaven until Lottie is soothed. She adopts Lottie as her "little girl" from that afternoon on.
4.modern-da: Sara overvejer, at hendes behagelige liv aldrig rigtigt har prøvet hendes karakter — hun undrer sig over, om hun i hemmelighed kunne være et frygteligt barn. Hun beroligende Lottie, der skriger, ved at sætte sig ved siden af hende på gulvet og indrømme, at hun heller ikke har nogen mor, og finder derefter på en historie om himlen, til Lottie er trøstet. Fra den eftermiddag adopterer hun Lottie som sin »lille pige«.

5.modern-en: Sara catches sight of the scullery maid Becky listening hungrily to a story and defends her right to listen. Weeks later she finds Becky asleep in her armchair, wakes her gently, feeds her cake, and tells her: "We are just the same — I am only a little girl like you. It's just an accident that I am not you." She begins giving Becky regular story installments and food.
5.modern-da: Sara opdager køkkenpigen Becky, der lytter sultent til en historie, og forsvarer hendes ret til at lytte. Uger senere finder hun Becky sovende i sin lænestol, vækker hende forsigtigt, giver hende kage og siger: »Vi er præcis ens — jeg er bare en lille pige ligesom dig. Det er kun et tilfælde, at jeg ikke er dig.« Hun begynder at give Becky regelmæssige historieportioner og mad.

6.modern-en: On Sara's eleventh birthday, the school holds a grand party. Sara gives Becky permission to attend the unwrapping of the Last Doll by asking Miss Minchin as a birthday favor. She also intercepts Lavinia's taunts about being a princess, and answers publicly: "I pretend I am a princess so that I can try to behave like one." A worried letter from her father about the diamond mines casts a shadow over the celebrations.
6.modern-da: På Saras ellevte fødselsdag afholder skolen en stor fest. Sara sørger for, at Becky må overvære åbningen af Den Sidste Dukke, ved at bede Miss Minchin om det som en fødselsdagsgave. Hun afværger også Lavinias hån om prinsessespillet og svarer offentligt: »Jeg lader som om, jeg er en prinsesse, for at prøve at opføre mig som en.« Et bekymret brev fra hendes far om diamantminerne kaster en skygge over festen.

7.modern-en: While Sara's party is still underway, Mr. Barrow informs Miss Minchin that Captain Crewe is dead and penniless, the diamond mines a ruin. Miss Amelia finds Sara and tells her. Sara retreats to her room, whispers "My papa is dead!" to Emily over and over, then appears before Miss Minchin in her outgrown black dress and refuses to beg or thank her for the roof over her head — "You are not kind, and it is not a home." She is sent to the attic.
7.modern-da: Mens Saras fest stadig er i gang, oplyser Mr. Barrow Miss Minchin om, at kaptajn Crewe er død og ruineret, diamantminerne en fallit. Miss Amelia finder Sara og fortæller hende det. Sara trækker sig tilbage til sit værelse, hvisker »Min far er død!« til Emily igen og igen, og viser sig derefter for Miss Minchin i sin for lille sorte kjole og nægter at tigge eller takke hende for taget over hovedet — »Du er ikke venlig, og det er ikke et hjem.« Hun sendes til kvisten.

8.modern-en: Sara spends her first night in the freezing attic with only Emily, hearing rats in the walls and telling herself over and over that her father is dead. Within days she is turned into an errand girl and servant. She consoles herself with the princess idea: "If I am a princess in rags and tatters, I can be a princess inside." Ermengarde comes to find her, and Sara reconciles with her friend by making the attic into the Bastille.
8.modern-da: Sara tilbringer sin første nat på den iskolde kvist med kun Emily, hørende rotter i væggene og gentager for sig selv, at hendes far er død. Inden for dage gøres hun til budbud og tjener. Hun trøster sig med prinsesseideen: »Hvis jeg er en prinsesse i pjalter, kan jeg være en prinsesse indeni.« Ermengarde finder hende, og Sara forsoner sig med veninden ved at gøre kvisten til Bastillen.

9.modern-en: Lottie finds the attic on her own and is frightened by its bareness; Sara transforms the room through storytelling, making Lottie see chimneys and sparrows and a cozy nest. Alone afterward, Sara first meets the large rat she will call Melchisedec, sits very still until he takes crumbs from near her feet, and decides he must be her Bastille companion. When Ermengarde visits, Sara introduces Melchisedec by name.
9.modern-da: Lottie finder kvisten på egen hånd og bliver bange over dens tomhed; Sara forvandler rummet gennem fortælling og får Lottie til at se skorstene, spurve og en hyggelig rede. Alene bagefter møder Sara for første gang den store rotte, hun vil kalde Melchisedec, sidder meget stille, til han tager smuler fra nærheden af hendes fødder, og beslutter, at han skal være hendes Bastille-kammerat. Da Ermengarde besøger hende, præsenterer Sara Melchisedec ved navn.

10.modern-en: Sara notices the family next door taking in a sick Indian gentleman's furniture, recognizes Indian teakwood pieces like her father owned, and begins watching the gentleman through his window by night, wishing him good night and sending "kind thoughts" through the glass. She also receives a touching moment when a small boy from the Large Family mistakes her for a beggar and gives her his Christmas sixpence — she keeps it on a ribbon around her neck.
10.modern-da: Sara bemærker familien ved siden af, der indretter en syg indisk herres hus, genkender indiske teaktræsmøbler ligesom dem, hendes far ejede, og begynder at kigge på herren gennem hans vindue om natten og ønske ham godnat og sende »venlige tanker« igennem glasset. Hun modtager også et rørende øjeblik, da en lille dreng fra Den Store Familie forveksler hende med en tigger og giver hende sin julesekspence — hun bærer den på et bånd om halsen.

11.modern-en: Sara meets Ram Dass on the roof when his monkey escapes into her attic. She speaks Hindustani to him, wins his respect, and lets him retrieve the monkey. Alone afterward, she draws herself up and reminds herself: whatever comes, she can still be a princess inside — like Marie Antoinette in prison. When Miss Minchin boxes her ears in the schoolroom for daydreaming, Sara tells her calmly that she was thinking about what would happen if Miss Minchin discovered Sara really was a princess.
11.modern-da: Sara møder Ram Dass på taget, da hans abe stikker af ind på hendes kvist. Hun taler hindustani til ham, vinder hans respekt og lader ham hente aben. Alene bagefter retter hun ryggen og minder sig selv om: hvad der end sker, kan hun stadig være en prinsesse indeni — som Marie Antoinette i fængslet. Da Miss Minchin slår hende i skolestuen for dagdrømmeri, fortæller Sara hende roligt, at hun tænkte på, hvad der ville ske, hvis Miss Minchin opdagede, at Sara virkelig var en prinsesse.

12.modern-en: Sara watches Mr. Carrisford through the wall and concludes he has a present trouble on his mind, not just a past one. She has heard from the kitchen that his misfortunes involved mines. Through the wall she hears Carrisford tell Carmichael he cannot forget the child of Captain Crewe — not knowing that very child sits on the other side, murmuring to herself: "What a long time it seems since I was your Little Missus!"
12.modern-da: Sara iagttager Mr. Carrisford gennem væggen og konkluderer, at han har en nuværende bekymring, ikke blot en fortid. Fra køkkenet har hun hørt, at hans uheld involverede miner. Gennem væggen hører hun Carrisford fortælle Carmichael, at han ikke kan glemme kaptajn Crewes barn — uden at vide, at netop det barn sidder på den anden side og hvisker: »Det er så lang tid siden, jeg var din Lille Frue!«

13.modern-en: On a freezing, rainy day when Sara has had no dinner and is sent out on one errand after another, she finds a fourpenny piece in the gutter outside a baker's shop. She goes inside to ask if the owner has lost it, then uses it to buy buns — but when she sees a starving child on the steps, she gives away five of her six buns, keeping only one for herself. The baker-woman watches in wonder.
13.modern-da: På en frysende, regnfuld dag, da Sara ikke har fået middag og sendes ud på en ærinde efter det andet, finder hun en firepencemønt i rendestenen foran en bagerbutik. Hun går ind for at spørge, om ejeren har mistet den, og bruger den derefter til at købe boller — men da hun ser et udsultet barn på trappen, giver hun fem af sine seks boller bort og beholder kun én til sig selv. Bakerkonen ser til med forundring.

14.modern-en: Sara is out on errands while Ram Dass and Carrisford's secretary secretly enter the attic and take detailed notes on everything it lacks — the hard bed, the empty grate, the bare floor. She knows nothing of this, and returns exhausted to the cold room.
14.modern-da: Sara er ude på ærinder, mens Ram Dass og Carrisford sekretær hemmeligt træder ind på kvisten og noterer omhyggeligt alt, hvad den mangler — den hårde seng, den tomme grille, det bare gulv. Hun ved intet om dette og vender udmatttet tilbage til det kolde rum.

15.modern-en: After a disastrous attic banquet — with Ermengarde and Becky — is broken up by Miss Minchin, who sentences Sara to no meals the next day, Sara falls asleep on the old mattress in despair. She wakes to find the attic transformed: a blazing fire, warm bedding, a supper laid for two, books, cushions, a lamp. She touches everything to prove she is not dreaming, then wakes Becky to share it. "The Magic has come," she says. "The worst thing never quite comes."
15.modern-da: Efter at et katastrofalt kvistbanket — med Ermengarde og Becky — afbrydes af Miss Minchin, der dømmer Sara til ingen måltider næste dag, falder Sara i søvn på den gamle madras i fortvivlelse. Hun vågner til at finde kvisten forvandlet: en blusende ild, varmt sengetøj, et aftensmåltid dækket til to, bøger, puder, en lampe. Hun rører ved alt for at bevise, at hun ikke drømmer, og vækker derefter Becky for at dele det. »Magien er kommet,« siger hun. »Det værste sker aldrig helt.«

16.modern-en: Sara walks into school the next morning glowing with warmth and food, mystifying Miss Minchin who expected a broken child. She decides to keep the magic a secret and writes a thank-you letter to her unknown friend. Packages of new clothes arrive addressed to her; Miss Minchin, baffled, allows her to dress well and come downstairs again — and the whole school stares at the returned "Princess Sara." The monkey escapes again and Sara brings him back.
16.modern-da: Sara går på skolen næste morgen strålende af varme og mad, til stor forvirring for Miss Minchin, der forventede et knust barn. Hun beslutter at holde magien hemmelig og skriver et takkebrev til sin ukendte ven. Pakker med nye tøj ankommer adresseret til hende; Miss Minchin, forvirret, tillader hende at klæde sig pænt og komme ned igen — og hele skolen stirrer på den tilbagevendte »Prinsesse Sara«. Aben stikker af igen, og Sara bringer ham tilbage.

17.modern-en: Sara brings the monkey back to Carrisford's house and, speaking Hindustani, mentions she was born in India. Carrisford sits upright as if struck. She tells him her father died in India after losing his fortune to a trusted friend. When she says his name — Captain Crewe — Carrisford gasps, "It is the child!" Sara, bewildered, asks Mr. Carmichael: "What child am I?"
17.modern-da: Sara bringer aben tilbage til Carrisford hus og nævner på hindustani, at hun er født i Indien. Carrisford rejser sig op som ramt af et slag. Hun fortæller ham, at hendes far døde i Indien efter at have mistet sin formue til en betroet ven. Da hun siger hans navn — kaptajn Crewe — udstøder Carrisford: »Det er barnet!« Sara spørger forvirret Mr. Carmichael: »Hvad barn er jeg?«

18.modern-en: Sara learns the full truth from Mrs. Carmichael: Carrisford was her father's friend, not a villain — he had suffered brain fever and genuinely believed the fortune lost. She refuses Miss Minchin's attempt to reclaim her, looking her steadily in the face: "You know quite well why I will not go home with you." When Miss Minchin taunts that she must feel like a princess again, Sara answers quietly: "I tried not to be anything else — even when I was coldest and hungriest."
18.modern-da: Sara hører den fulde sandhed fra Mrs. Carmichael: Carrisford var hendes fars ven, ikke en skurk — han havde lidt hjernefeber og troede oprigtigt, at formuen var tabt. Hun afviser Miss Minchins forsøg på at genvinde hende og ser hende fast i øjnene: »Du ved godt, hvorfor jeg ikke vil komme hjem med dig.« Da Miss Minchin håner, at hun vist føler sig som prinsesse igen, svarer Sara stille: »Jeg prøvede på aldrig at være noget andet — selv da jeg var koldest og sultest.«

19.modern-en: Sara settles into life with Carrisford, who becomes her guardian and "Uncle Tom." She tells the Large Family the story of the magic banquet. She asks Carrisford's permission to set up a scheme with the baker-woman to feed hungry street children on bad days, funding it herself — "I know what it is to be hungry, and it is very hard when you cannot even pretend it away." She also finds Anne, the beggar-child she once fed, now working happily in the bakery.
19.modern-da: Sara slår sig ned hos Carrisford, der bliver hendes formynder og »Onkel Tom«. Hun fortæller Den Store Familie historien om det magiske banket. Hun beder Carrisford om tilladelse til at oprette en ordning med bagerinden om at fodre sultne gadeborn på dårlige dage, finansieret af hende selv — »Jeg ved, hvad det vil sige at være sulten, og det er meget svært, når man ikke engang kan bilde sig det væk.« Hun finder også Anne, det tiggerbarn, hun engang fodrede, som nu arbejder lykkeligt i bageriet.

1.modern-en: Captain Crewe brings Sara from India to Miss Minchin's school, clearly dreading the separation. He buys her an extravagant wardrobe and the doll Emily, watches her asleep in the night and whispers that she will never know how much her daddy will miss her. After a last goodbye in which she tells him he is "inside my heart," he drives away waving from the cab.
1.modern-da: Kaptajn Crewe bringer Sara fra Indien til Miss Minchins skole og frygter tydeligt adskillelsen. Han køber hende en overdådig garderobe og dukken Emily, ser hende sove om natten og hvisker, at hun aldrig vil vide, hvor meget hendes far vil savne hende. Efter en sidste afsked, hvor hun fortæller ham, at han er »i mit hjerte«, kører han væk og vinker fra droschen.

6.modern-en: A letter arrives from Captain Crewe for Sara's birthday, written in a less buoyant tone than usual — he is unwell and troubled by the business connected with the diamond mines. He has sent the Last Doll as a birthday gift and jokes that his little missus would give him good advice if she were there.
6.modern-da: Et brev ankommer fra kaptajn Crewe til Saras fødselsdag, skrevet i en mindre oplivet tone end sædvanlig — han er syg og tynget af forretninger forbundet med diamantminerne. Han har sendt Den Sidste Dukke som fødselsdagsgave og joker om, at hans lille frue ville give ham gode råd, hvis hun var der.

7.modern-en: Mr. Barrow announces that Captain Crewe has died — of jungle fever and the shock of the mine disaster combined. He died delirious, raving about his little girl, and left not a penny. He never knew his fortune would eventually be recovered.
7.modern-da: Mr. Barrow meddeler, at kaptajn Crewe er død — af jungelfeber og chokket over minedisastren tilsammen. Han døde vildfarende, rasende om sin lille pige, og efterlod ikke en øre. Han vidste aldrig, at hans formue til sidst ville blive genvundet.

12.modern-en: Captain Crewe is present only in memory and in the vision that haunts Carrisford — who dreams of him asking "Tom, old man — where is the Little Missus?" Sara, on the other side of the wall, murmurs to herself how long it has been since she was her papa's Little Missus.
12.modern-da: Kaptajn Crewe er kun til stede i erindringen og i det syn, der hjemsøger Carrisford — som drømmer om ham, der spørger: »Tom, gamle ven — hvor er den Lille Frue?« Sara, på den anden side af væggen, mumler for sig selv, hvor lang tid det er siden, hun var sin fars Lille Frue.

17.modern-en: Captain Crewe's name, spoken aloud by Sara — "His name was Ralph Crewe. Captain Crewe. He died in India" — triggers Carrisford's collapse of recognition. He is the lost child's dead father, the friend Carrisford has grieved for years. His story, told simply by Sara, is the pivot on which the whole resolution turns.
17.modern-da: Kaptajn Crewes navn, udtalt højt af Sara — »Hans navn var Ralph Crewe. Kaptajn Crewe. Han døde i Indien« — udløser Carrisfords sammenbrud af genkendelse. Han er det forsvundne barns døde far, vennen Carrisford har sørget over i årevis. Hans historie, fortalt simpelt af Sara, er omdrejningspunktet, som hele opløsningen drejer sig om.

1.modern-en: Miss Minchin receives Sara and Captain Crewe with elaborate flattery, calling Sara a beautiful and promising child — a lie Sara sees through at once. She learns that Sara is to have a pony, a maid, and great privilege. Sara thinks Miss Minchin is exactly like her house: tall, dull, respectable, and ugly.
1.modern-da: Miss Minchin modtager Sara og kaptajn Crewe med overdrevet smiger og kalder Sara et smukt og lovende barn — en løgn, Sara gennemskuer straks. Hun erfarer, at Sara skal have en pony, en tjener og store privilegier. Sara synes, Miss Minchin ligner hendes hus: høj, kedelig, respektabel og grim.

2.modern-en: Miss Minchin silences Sara twice when she tries to explain she already speaks French, then is humiliated when Monsieur Dufarge reveals the truth. From that day she nurses a grudge against her show pupil, resenting her cleverness.
2.modern-da: Miss Minchin tier Sara ihjel to gange, da hun forsøger at forklare, at hun allerede taler fransk, og ydmyges derefter, da Monsieur Dufarge afslører sandheden. Fra den dag nærer hun nag til sin paradepensionist og misunder hendes klogskab.

4.modern-en: Miss Minchin is driven out of the room by Lottie's screaming fit and grateful when Sara offers to quiet her. She allows Sara to attempt it, but frames it as a favor rather than a sign of Sara's ability.
4.modern-da: Miss Minchin drives ud af rummet af Lotties skrigeanfald og er taknemmelig, da Sara tilbyder at berolige hende. Hun lader Sara prøve, men fremstiller det som en gunst snarere end et tegn på Saras evner.

5.modern-en: Miss Minchin is aware that Sara is kind to Becky but knows nothing of the depth of their friendship. She continues using Sara as a show pupil, having her speak French to visiting parents and parading her as a credit to the seminary.
5.modern-da: Miss Minchin er klar over, at Sara er venlig over for Becky, men ved intet om dybden i deres venskab. Hun bruger fortsat Sara som paradepensionist, lader hende tale fransk for besøgende forældre og fremviser hende som en kredit for pensionatet.

6.modern-en: Miss Minchin delivers an embarrassing speech on Sara's birthday, lavishing public praise that Miss Minchin means as self-advertisement. Sara finds the praise about money particularly hateful.
6.modern-da: Miss Minchin holder en pinlig tale på Saras fødselsdag og øser ros over hende, som egentlig er ment som selvreklamering. Sara synes, at prisen om penge er særlig afskyelig.

7.modern-en: Upon learning of Captain Crewe's death and ruin from Mr. Barrow, Miss Minchin erupts in rage — not grief — at the loss of her star patron and unpaid bills. She strips Sara of her rooms and privileges immediately, commands her to dress in the outgrown black dress, and sets her conditions for keeping her: work, errands, and teaching the little ones in exchange for a roof over her head.
7.modern-da: Da Miss Minchin fra Mr. Barrow erfarer om kaptajn Crewes død og ruin, udbyder hun i raseri — ikke sorg — over tabet af sin parademecenat og de ubetalte regninger. Hun berøver straks Sara hendesværelser og privilegier, beordrer hende til at klæde sig i den for lille sorte kjole og sætter sine betingelser for at beholde hende: arbejde, ærinder og undervisning af de mindste til gengæld for et tag over hovedet.

8.modern-en: Miss Minchin implements Sara's new life with cold efficiency. She forbids Sara to form close friendships with the other girls, preferring her to live a separate life suited to her new circumstances — partly to prevent a "mistreated heroine" narrative from reaching parents.
8.modern-da: Miss Minchin iværksætter Saras nye liv med kold effektivitet. Hun forbyder Sara at danne nære venskaber med de andre piger og foretrækker, at hun lever et adskilt liv, der passer til hendes nye omstændigheder — delvis for at forhindre en »mishandlet heltinde«-fortælling i at nå forældrene.

11.modern-en: Miss Minchin boxes Sara's ears in the schoolroom for daydreaming, then demands that Sara beg her pardon. When Sara answers with quiet dignity that she will not apologize for thinking, and calmly implies that Miss Minchin does not know what she is doing, Miss Minchin orders her from the room in a rage.
11.modern-da: Miss Minchin slår Sara i øret i skolestuen for dagdrømmeri og kræver derefter, at Sara beder om undskyldning. Da Sara svarer med rolig værdighed, at hun ikke vil undskylde for at tænke, og roligt antyder, at Miss Minchin ikke ved, hvad hun gør, beordrer Miss Minchin hende rasende ud af rummet.

15.modern-en: Miss Minchin discovers the attic party, boxes Becky's ears and threatens to dismiss her, confiscates the food, punishes Ermengarde, and sentences Sara to no meals for the next day. She seethes with contempt at Sara's strange dignity under punishment. Lavinia had informed on them.
15.modern-da: Miss Minchin opdager kvistfesten, slår Becky i øret og truer med at afskedige hende, konfiskerer maden, straffer Ermengarde og dømmer Sara til ingen måltider næste dag. Hun koger af foragt over Saras mærkelige værdighed under straf. Lavinia havde sladret om dem.

16.modern-en: Miss Minchin is baffled to find Sara glowing with health the morning after the punishment, not broken. When mysterious clothing parcels arrive addressed to Sara, Miss Minchin's suspicion of an influential unknown patron makes her suddenly treat Sara with cold correctness.
16.modern-da: Miss Minchin er forvirret over at finde Sara strålende af sundhed morgenen efter straffen, ikke knust. Da mystiske tøjpakker ankommer adresseret til Sara, får Miss Minchins mistanke om en indflydelsesrig ukendt beskytter hende til pludselig at behandle Sara med kold korrekthed.

17.modern-en: Miss Minchin does not appear directly but is described by Sara to Carrisford: Sara now sleeps in the attic, runs errands for the cook, and does whatever she is told.
17.modern-da: Miss Minchin optræder ikke direkte, men beskrives af Sara over for Carrisford: Sara sover nu på kvisten, løber ærinder for kokken og gør, hvad hun bliver bedt om.

18.modern-en: Miss Minchin arrives at Carrisford's house to reclaim Sara and is told by Mr. Carmichael that Sara's fortune has been recovered and multiplied by the diamond mines. She makes a desperate attempt to retain Sara by claiming she always loved her — Sara answers with a quiet stare: "I did not know that." Returning home, she is harangued by Miss Amelia, who tells her to her face that she was a hard, worldly woman who treated a clever, good child badly.
18.modern-da: Miss Minchin ankommer til Carrisford hus for at genvinde Sara og får at vide af Mr. Carmichael, at Saras formue er genvundet og mangedoblet af diamantminerne. Hun forsøger desperat at beholde Sara ved at hævde, at hun altid har elsket hende — Sara svarer med et stille blik: »Det vidste jeg ikke.« Da hun vender hjem, udskælder Miss Amelia hende og siger hende lige i ansigtet, at hun var en hård, verdslig kvinde, der behandlede et klogt, godt barn dårligt.

epithet.en: The scullery maid in the attic

5.modern-en: Becky is first seen creeping into the schoolroom to clean the grate while Sara tells a story, slipping into a trance of listening until her brush falls from her hand. When she is spotted and ordered out, Sara defends her right to listen. Later Sara finds Becky asleep in her armchair, wakes her gently, and treats her as a friend — feeding her cake and promising to tell her stories regularly.
5.modern-da: Becky ses første gang, da hun lister ind i skolestuen for at rengøre grillristen, mens Sara fortæller en historie, og glider ind i en trance af lytning, til hendes børste falder ud af hende. Da hun opdages og beordres ud, forsvarer Sara hendes ret til at lytte. Senere finder Sara Becky sovende i sin lænestol, vækker hende forsigtigt og behandler hende som en ven — fodrer hende med kage og lover at fortælle hende historier regelmæssigt.

6.modern-en: Becky has made Sara a birthday pincushion out of old red flannel, with black pins spelling "Menny hapy returns." It is crude and shows great effort. She used a discarded card from Miss Amelia's dustbin to make it seem proper. Sara hugs her and says "I love you, Becky — I do, I do!"
6.modern-da: Becky har lavet Sara et fødselsdagsnappenålspude af gammelt rødt flannel med sorte nåle, der staver »Menny hapy returns«. Det er primitivt og viser stor anstrengelse. Hun brugte et kasseret kort fra Miss Amelias skraldespand for at gøre det ordentligt. Sara omfavner hende og siger: »Jeg elsker dig, Becky — jeg gør, jeg gør!«

7.modern-en: Becky hides under the table during Barrow's visit, hears everything about Sara's ruin, and cannot stop herself from weeping when Miss Minchin discovers her. She begs Miss Minchin to be allowed to wait on Sara in her poverty — is refused — and runs to her attic in tears. She comes to Sara's attic door that night and tells her through broken sobs: "Whatever happens to you — you'd be a princess all the same."
7.modern-da: Becky gemmer sig under bordet under Barrows besøg, hører alt om Saras ruin og kan ikke holde sig fra at græde, da Miss Minchin opdager hende. Hun bønfalder Miss Minchin om lov til at betjene Sara i hendes fattigdom — nægtes — og løber grædende til sin kvist. Hun kommer til Saras kvistsælge den aften og fortæller hende gennem brudte hulk: »Hvad der end sker med dig — du ville altid være en prinsesse.«

8.modern-en: Becky becomes Sara's closest companion in misery. She slips into Sara's attic before dawn to help her dress, and knocks on the wall between their rooms at night. Their shared Bastille game — Sara as one prisoner, Becky as the next — gives both of them something to hold onto.
8.modern-da: Becky bliver Saras nærmeste selskab i elendighed. Hun lister ind på Saras kvist inden daggry for at hjælpe hende med at klæde sig på, og banker på væggen mellem deres rum om natten. Deres fælles Bastille-spil — Sara som én fange, Becky som den næste — giver dem begge noget at holde fast i.

9.modern-en: Becky communicates with Sara through their shared wall using a knocking code — two knocks meaning "are you there?" three for "yes," four for "good night." Ermengarde, watching, exclaims it is like a story; Sara answers: "It IS a story. Everything's a story."
9.modern-da: Becky kommunikerer med Sara gennem deres fælles væg ved hjælp af en bakkode — to bank, der betyder »er du der?«, tre for »ja«, fire for »god nat«. Ermengarde, der ser til, udbryder, at det er som en historie; Sara svarer: »Det ER en historie. Alt er en historie.«

13.modern-en: Becky appears only in the cold-weather description of their shared life — she is driven "like a little slave" during winter, and tells Sara the Bastille pretend is the only thing keeping her going.
13.modern-da: Becky optræder kun i beskrivelsen af deres fælles liv i koldt vejr — hun drives »som en lille slave« om vinteren og fortæller Sara, at Bastille-legen er det eneste, der holder hende kørende.

15.modern-en: Becky is invited to the attic party by Sara and shares in the feast. She is scolded and slapped by Miss Minchin when the party is discovered — wrongly accused of stealing a meat pie that day. When Sara wakes to find the magic room, she immediately goes to Becky's door to bring her in to share it.
15.modern-da: Becky inviteres til kvistfesten af Sara og deler i festen. Hun skældes ud og slås af Miss Minchin, da festen opdages — fejlagtigt beskyldt for at have stjålet en kødpaj den dag. Da Sara vågner og finder det magiske rum, går hun straks til Beckys dør for at bringe hende ind for at dele det.

16.modern-en: Becky gains a new mattress, pillow, supper, and fire through the magic — her attic is quietly improved each night alongside Sara's. The two share their suppers by the fire. Becky asks: "Do you think it could melt away, miss?" and hastily cramps food into her mouth in case it does.
16.modern-da: Becky får en ny madras, pude, aftensmad og ild gennem magien — hendes kvist forbedres stille og roligt om natten side om side med Saras. De to deler aftensmad ved ilden. Becky spørger: »Tror du, det kan smelte bort, frøken?« og stopper hurtigt mad i munden, i tilfælde af at det gør.

17.modern-en: Becky does not appear directly but is mentioned when Sara describes her life to Carrisford — Sara explains she sleeps next to the scullery maid and teaches the little ones.
17.modern-da: Becky optræder ikke direkte, men nævnes, da Sara beskriver sit liv for Carrisford — Sara forklarer, at hun sover ved siden af køkkenpigen og underviser de mindste.

18.modern-en: When the news of Sara's fortune reaches the school, Becky goes upstairs to say goodbye to the magic room — only to find Ram Dass there, the fire still burning, a letter from Sara, and the news that she is to come to Carrisford's house as Sara's personal attendant.
18.modern-da: Da nyheden om Saras formue når skolen, går Becky op for at sige farvel til det magiske rum — kun for at finde Ram Dass der, ilden stadig brændende, et brev fra Sara og nyheden om, at hun skal komme til Carrisfords hus som Saras personlige tjener.

19.modern-en: Becky is now Sara's attendant and accompanies her to the carriage with a pink, round, well-fed face — visible to Miss Minchin from her window, which Miss Minchin finds particularly irritating.
19.modern-da: Becky er nu Saras tjener og ledsager hende til droschen med et lyserødt, rundt, velforet ansigt — synligt for Miss Minchin fra hendes vindue, hvilket Miss Minchin finder særlig irriterende.

3.modern-en: Ermengarde watches Sara's French revelation with round-eyed amazement, then finds herself invited upstairs to meet Emily. She is fascinated by Sara's world of pretending and imaginings — her first encounter with anyone who makes things real by believing in them. She asks Sara to be best friends and is accepted.
3.modern-da: Ermengarde overværer Saras franske afsløring med store øjne af forundring og inviteres derefter op for at møde Emily. Hun er fascineret af Saras verden af leg og forestillinger — hendes første møde med nogen, der gør ting virkelige ved at tro på dem. Hun beder Sara om at være bedste venner og bliver accepteret.

4.modern-en: Ermengarde is mentioned as Sara's companion and study partner — Sara helps her with lessons and tells her stories, while Ermengarde brings Sara the gift of simple, uncritical affection.
4.modern-da: Ermengarde nævnes som Saras kammerat og studiekammerart — Sara hjælper hende med lektier og fortæller hende historier, mens Ermengarde giver Sara gaven af enkel, ukritisk hengivenhed.

6.modern-en: Ermengarde is among the children who listen to Sara tell stories about the diamond mines, delighting in the pictures Sara paints of sparkling underground passages.
6.modern-da: Ermengarde er blandt de born, der lytter til Sara fortælle historier om diamantminerne og fryder sig over de billeder, Sara maler af funklende underjordiske gange.

7.modern-en: At the birthday party, Ermengarde rushes forward to examine the Last Doll's accessories with everyone else, delighted and absorbed. She has no idea yet what is about to happen.
7.modern-da: Til fødselsdagsfesten iler Ermengarde frem for at undersøge Den Sidste Dukkes tilbehør med alle de andre, henrykt og opslugt. Hun aner endnu ikke, hvad der er ved at ske.

8.modern-en: After Sara's fall, Ermengarde returns from a visit home and greets Sara awkwardly in the corridor — she says "Oh — how are you?" and Sara asks in return, then walks past her. Weeks of estrangement follow, until Ermengarde creeps to the attic by candlelight and, with tears and a red shawl, asks Sara why she doesn't like her anymore.
8.modern-da: Efter Saras fald vender Ermengarde tilbage fra et hjemmebesøg og hilser klodset på Sara i gangen — hun siger »Åh — hvordan har du det?« og Sara svarer og går forbi hende. Uger med fremmedgørelse følger, til Ermengarde lister op på kvisten med levende lys og, med tårer og et rødt sjal, spørger Sara, hvorfor hun ikke kan lide hende mere.

9.modern-en: Ermengarde comes secretly to the attic and is introduced to Melchisedec — she is terrified and jumps onto the bed with her feet tucked up, but Sara coaxes her to watch. She begins to understand the Bastille game better and asks to be allowed to visit regularly.
9.modern-da: Ermengarde kommer hemmeligt til kvisten og præsenteres for Melchisedec — hun er bange og hopper op på sengen med fødderne trukket op under sig, men Sara lokker hende til at se til. Hun begynder at forstå Bastille-spillet bedre og beder om tilladelse til at besøge regelmæssigt.

12.modern-en: Ermengarde is mentioned only in passing as one of Sara's two companions in the attic — her visits are rare because of the risk, and Sara lives mostly alone.
12.modern-da: Ermengarde nævnes kun flygtigt som en af Saras to kammerat er på kvisten — hendes besøg er sjældne på grund af risikoen, og Sara lever mest alene.

15.modern-en: Ermengarde brings her hamper from her aunt to the attic and proposes the party. When Miss Minchin discovers them, Ermengarde bursts into tears and pleads — "we're only having a party" — but is sent away with the books under her arm and told her father will be written to.
15.modern-da: Ermengarde bringer sin kurv fra sin tante til kvisten og foreslår festen. Da Miss Minchin opdager dem, bryder Ermengarde ud i gråd og bønfalder — »vi holder bare fest« — men sendes væk med bøgerne under armen og besked om, at hendes far vil blive skrevet til.

18.modern-en: Ermengarde receives Sara's letter describing everything that has happened and reads it aloud to the assembled schoolroom in a kind of half-stunned wonder — "There WERE diamond mines. There WERE!" She is to be allowed to visit Sara next door.
18.modern-da: Ermengarde modtager Saras brev, der beskriver alt, hvad der er sket, og læser det højt for den forsamlede skolestue i en slags halvbedøvet forundring — »Der VAR diamantminer. Der VAR!« Hun skal have lov til at besøge Sara ved siden af.

19.modern-en: Ermengarde is among those who come to the Indian gentleman's house to hear Sara tell the story of the magic banquet. She is now free to visit whenever she likes.
19.modern-da: Ermengarde er blandt dem, der kommer til den indiske herres hus for at høre Sara fortælle historien om det magiske banket. Hun er nu fri til at besøge, når det passer hende.

4.modern-en: Lottie is in the middle of a howling fit — kicking on the floor, screaming about having no mama — when Sara comes in, sits beside her, and simply says "Neither have I." Lottie is so startled she stops crying. Sara tells her about heaven and offers to be her school-mama. Lottie accepts with dimpling delight.
4.modern-da: Lottie er midt i et hylende anfald — sparker på gulvet og skriger om ikke at have nogen mor — da Sara kommer ind, sætter sig ved siden af hende og simpelthen siger: »Det har jeg heller ikke.« Lottie er så overrasket, at hun holder op med at græde. Sara fortæller hende om himlen og tilbyder at være hendes skolemor. Lottie accepterer med smilende glæde.

5.modern-en: Lottie passes on what she has heard about Sara's princess-pretend to Lavinia, without realizing she is providing ammunition against Sara. She also loyally defends Sara's dead mother: "Sara's mama knows everything. So does my mama."
5.modern-da: Lottie videregiver, hvad hun har hørt om Saras prinsesselegespil til Lavinia, uden at indse, at hun leverer ammunition mod Sara. Hun forsvarer også loyalt Saras afdøde mor: »Saras mor ved alt. Det gør min mor også.«

6.modern-en: When Lottie falls and scrapes her knee at the birthday party and dissolves into wailing, Sara holds her and calms her with the promise of a story about the diamond mines. She mothers Lottie smoothly despite the interruption to her own absorbed reading.
6.modern-da: Da Lottie falder og skraber knæet til fødselsdagsfesten og smelter ind i klynken, holder Sara hende og beroliger hende med løftet om en historie om diamantminerne. Hun modrer Lottie smertefrit på trods af afbrydelsen af sin egen fordybede læsning.

9.modern-en: Lottie traces Sara to the attic on her own, is briefly horrified by its bareness, but is won over when Sara climbs the table and they look out the skylight at sparrows and chimneys. Lottie produces bun-crumbs from her pocket and helps Sara coax sparrows to come eat.
9.modern-da: Lottie sporer Sara til kvisten på egen hånd, er kortvarigt rystet over dens tomhed, men vindes over, da Sara klatrer op på bordet og de kigger ud af tagvinduet på spurve og skorstene. Lottie hiver bulle-smuler op af lommen og hjælper Sara med at lokke spurve til at komme og spise.

10.modern-en: Lottie whispers to Sara during French class that the Indian gentleman next door looks yellow — "Do you think he is a Chinee?" Sara shushes her gently and gets on with the lesson.
10.modern-da: Lottie hvisker til Sara under fransklektionen, at den indiske herre ved siden af ser gul ud — »Tror du, han er kineser?« Sara beder hende stille blidt og fortsætter lektionen.

16.modern-en: Lottie is mentioned as one of the children Sara helps with lessons in secret — Sara sometimes helps her sums by candlelight. Miss Minchin cannot understand why Lottie is suddenly doing well.
16.modern-da: Lottie nævnes som et af de børn, Sara hemmeligt hjælper med lektier — Sara hjælper hende indimellem med regning ved stearinlysets skær. Miss Minchin kan ikke forstå, hvorfor Lottie pludselig klarer sig godt.

18.modern-en: When Ermengarde reads Sara's letter aloud to the schoolroom, Lottie is among those who hear it and begins to cry — the news is overwhelming. She will be allowed to visit Sara next door.
18.modern-da: Da Ermengarde læser Saras brev højt for skolestuen, er Lottie blandt dem, der hører det og begynder at græde — nyheden er overvældende. Hun vil få lov til at besøge Sara ved siden af.

19.modern-en: Lottie comes to the Indian gentleman's house with Ermengarde and the Large Family to hear Sara tell the story of the magic. She is among those who get to celebrate with Sara in her new home.
19.modern-da: Lottie kommer til den indiske herres hus med Ermengarde og Den Store Familie for at høre Sara fortælle historien om magien. Hun er blandt dem, der fejrer Saras nye hjem.

epithet.en: The ill man searching for the lost child
epithet.da: Den syge mand, der leder efter det forsvundne barn

10.modern-en: Mr. Carrisford arrives at the house next door — haggard, wrapped in furs, carried up the steps by servants. Sara watches through the window and concludes he looks like a man who has a present trouble on his mind, not merely past ones. She begins to watch him nightly and send him wordless "good nights" through the glass.
10.modern-da: Mr. Carrisford ankommer til huset ved siden af — udmattet, pakket ind i pelsmuffer, båret op ad trapperne af tjenere. Sara kigger ind gennem vinduet og konkluderer, at han ligner en mand, der har en nutidig bekymring, ikke blot fortidige. Hun begynder at iagttage ham om natten og sende ham stumme »god natter« gennem glasset.

11.modern-en: Carrisford is mentioned only through Ram Dass's description — he is ill and sometimes amused by the monkey, who belongs to him.
11.modern-da: Carrisford nævnes kun gennem Ram Dass's beskrivelse — han er syg og sommetider underholdt af aben, der tilhører ham.

12.modern-en: Carrisford tells Carmichael that the fortune he believed lost has been recovered, but he cannot recover his own health or conscience while he believes Captain Crewe's daughter is lost and possibly suffering. He dreams of Crewe asking "where is the Little Missus?" and clings to Carmichael's hand: "I must be able to answer him."
12.modern-da: Carrisford fortæller Carmichael, at den formue, han troede var tabt, er genvundet, men han kan ikke genvinde sit eget helbred eller samvittighed, mens han tror, at kaptajn Crewes datter er forsvundet og måske lider. Han drømmer om Crewe, der spørger: »Hvor er den Lille Frue?« og klamrer sig til Carmichaels hånd: »Jeg må kunne svare ham.«

14.modern-en: Carrisford plans and finances the secret transformation of Sara's attic — he listens to Ram Dass's accounts of Sara's hardship and takes pleasure in devising ways to help her, partly to distract himself from illness. His secretary and Ram Dass survey the attic while Sara is out.
14.modern-da: Carrisford planlægger og finansierer den hemmelige forvandling af Saras kvist — han lytter til Ram Dass's beretninger om Saras nød og finder glæde i at udtænke måder at hjælpe hende på, delvis for at aflede sig selv fra sin sygdom. Hans sekretær og Ram Dass undersøger kvisten, mens Sara er ude.

15.modern-en: Carrisford is watching when Sara passes the house and catches Ram Dass closing the shutters. He is shown thinking about the lost girl Carmichael is searching for in Moscow — not yet knowing she is fifty feet away. Ram Dass reports to him that Sara is now glowing with warmth and food after a night in the transformed room.
15.modern-da: Carrisford ser til, da Sara passerer huset og fanger Ram Dass, der lukker skodder. Han ses tænkende på den forsvundne pige, Carmichael leder efter i Moskva — endnu ikke vidende om, at hun er halvtreds fod væk. Ram Dass rapporterer til ham, at Sara nu stråler af varme og mad efter en nat i det forvandlede rum.

16.modern-en: Carrisford notes that the child next door looks less thin and has color in her cheeks — his magic is working. He is described watching her pass by and feeling interest in her long before he knows who she is.
16.modern-da: Carrisford bemærker, at barnet ved siden af ser mindre tynd ud og har farve i kinderne — hans magi virker. Han beskrives som iagttagende, mens hun passerer forbi, og interesseret i hende længe inden han ved, hvem hun er.

17.modern-en: When Sara returns the monkey and mentions she was born in India, Carrisford sits upright with sudden fierce attention. She says her father was Captain Crewe and he gasps "It is the child!" — then collapses as Ram Dass gives him medicine. He cannot question her himself and asks Carmichael to do it.
17.modern-da: Da Sara bringer aben tilbage og nævner, at hun er født i Indien, rejser Carrisford sig med pludselig intens opmærksomhed. Hun siger, at hendes far var kaptajn Crewe, og han udstøder »Det er barnet!« — falder derefter sammen, mens Ram Dass giver ham medicin. Han kan ikke selv stille hende spørgsmål og beder Carmichael om at gøre det.

18.modern-en: Carrisford confirms he is Sara's guardian and friend, holds her hands in his the way her father did, and draws her to kneel beside his chair. He tells Miss Minchin that Sara is not going back — "Her home from now on will be with me." Carmichael tells his wife: "The man will be himself again in three weeks. Look at his face already."
18.modern-da: Carrisford bekræfter, at han er Saras formynder og ven, holder hendes hænder i sine ligesom hendes far plejede, og trækker hende til at knæle ved siden af hans stol. Han fortæller Miss Minchin, at Sara ikke kommer tilbage — »Hendes hjem fra nu af vil være hos mig.« Carmichael fortæller sin kone: »Manden vil være sig selv igen om tre uger. Se bare på hans ansigt allerede.«

19.modern-en: Carrisford — now Sara's "Uncle Tom" — and Sara sit together by the fire in the evenings; he loves these hours more than any others. When Sara tells him about the bun shop and the hungry child, he lets her set up her feeding scheme without hesitation: "You shall do it tomorrow morning." He draws her small dark head down on his knee and strokes her hair.
19.modern-da: Carrisford — nu Saras »Onkel Tom« — og Sara sidder sammen ved ilden om aftenerne; han elsker disse timer mere end nogen andre. Da Sara fortæller ham om bagerbutikken og det sultne barn, lader han hende oprette sin fødningsordning uden tøven: »Du skal gøre det i morgen tidlig.« Han trækker hendes lille mørke hoved ned på sit knæ og stryger hendes hår.

epithet.da: Lascaren på den anden side af muren

11.modern-en: Ram Dass first appears on the neighboring roof at sunset, holding his monkey and looking homesick. Sara speaks Hindustani to him; he is moved to tears. When the monkey escapes into the attic, Ram Dass crosses the roof slates with silent agility to retrieve it, bows to Sara with the courtesy due a rajah's daughter, and says nothing about the room's poverty.
11.modern-da: Ram Dass optræder første gang på naboens tag ved solnedgang, holdende sin abe og seende hjemvé. Sara taler hindustani til ham; han er rørt til tårer. Da aben stikker af ind på kvisten, krydser Ram Dass tagfladerne med stille smidighed for at hente den, bukker for Sara med den agtelse, der tilkommer en rajahs datter, og siger intet om rummets fattigdom.

12.modern-en: Ram Dass tells Carrisford about Sara in detail — her daily comings and goings, her sparrows, her rat, her attic. It was Ram Dass who first had the fancy of creeping across the roof to make her warm, and who told Carrisford about her to cheer him up. The plan to transform the attic grows from his imagination.
12.modern-da: Ram Dass fortæller Carrisford om Sara i detaljer — hendes daglige ud og ind, hendes spurve, hendes rotte, hendes kvist. Det var Ram Dass, der først fik den tanke at krybe over taget for at varme hende, og som fortalte Carrisford om hende for at opmuntre ham. Planen om at forvandle kvisten vokser ud af hans fantasi.

14.modern-en: Ram Dass enters the attic through the skylight with Carrisford's secretary to survey it for the transformation. He has already inserted small silent nails into the plaster walls in preparation. Melchisedec hides in terror as the two men take notes and plan in whispers.
14.modern-da: Ram Dass træder ind på kvisten gennem tagvinduet med Carrisfords sekretær for at undersøge den til forvandlingen. Han har allerede sat små stille søm i pudsevæggene som forberedelse. Melchisedec gemmer sig i rædsel, mens de to mænd tager noter og planlægger i hviske.

15.modern-en: Ram Dass executes the first magic transformation while Sara sleeps — creeping through the skylight, handing goods in through the window from his companion, arranging the room without a sound. He peeks in through the skylight twice during the evening to check.
15.modern-da: Ram Dass udfører den første magiske forvandling, mens Sara sover — lister ind gennem tagvinduet, modtager varer ind through vinduet fra sin kammerat, ordner rummet uden en lyd. Han kigger ind through tagvinduet to gange om aftenen for at tjekke.

16.modern-en: Ram Dass continues the nightly magic — adding new items, removing the supper remains, expanding the room's beauty. It is he who announces to Carrisford that Sara has come next door with the monkey.
16.modern-da: Ram Dass fortsætter den nattlige magi — tilføjer nye ting, fjerner aftensmadsresterne, udvider rummets skønhed. Det er ham, der meddeler Carrisford, at Sara er kommet ved siden af med aben.

17.modern-en: Ram Dass is present in the room when Sara tells her story; he tends Carrisford when the invalid collapses with recognition. Sara looks toward him when wondering whether to give back the monkey.
17.modern-da: Ram Dass er til stede i rummet, da Sara fortæller sin historie; han plejer Carrisford, da invaliden falder sammen af genkendelse. Sara kigger hen imod ham, da hun overvejer, om hun skal give aben tilbage.

18.modern-en: Ram Dass escorts Miss Minchin out of the room with a bow when she is dismissed. He also visits Becky's attic that final night with the lamp still burning and Sara's letter, to tell her she is to come as Sara's attendant — then slips back over the roof as silently as he arrived.
18.modern-da: Ram Dass eskorterer Miss Minchin ud af rummet med et bukken, da hun afskedigedes. Han besøger også Beckys kvist den sidste nat med lampen stadig brændende og Saras brev, for at fortælle hende, at hun skal komme som Saras tjener — glider derefter tilbage over taget lige så stille, som han kom.

9.modern-en: After Lottie leaves, Sara notices a large rat sitting up on his hind legs near the door, sniffing curiously at crumbs. She holds very still, thinks about how hard it must be to be a rat that nobody likes, and speaks to him gently until he darts in and takes the largest crumb. "I knew he wanted it for his children," she says. "I believe I could make friends with him."
9.modern-da: Efter at Lottie er gået, bemærker Sara en stor rotte, der sidder op på bagbenene nær døren og snuser nysgerrigt til smuler. Hun sidder meget stille, tænker over, hvor svært det må være at være en rotte, som ingen kan lide, og taler blidt til ham, til han pludselig tager det største stykke. »Jeg vidste, han ville have det til sine børn,« siger hun. »Jeg tror, jeg kunne blive ven med ham.«

10.modern-en: Melchisedec has become a regular visitor — Sara has learned to distinguish his wife's squeak from his own and the children's. She feeds him scraps from the kitchen and tells Ermengarde he is a "Bastille rat" sent to be her friend.
10.modern-da: Melchisedec er blevet en fast gæst — Sara har lært at skelne hans kones piben fra hans egen og børnenes. Hun fodrer ham med rester fra køkkenet og fortæller Ermengarde, at han er en »Bastille-rotte« sendt for at være hendes ven.

13.modern-en: Melchisedec appears on a dreadful cold evening as Sara returns to the attic starving and cold, and she has no crumbs to give him — she has forgotten because she was too wretched. He shuffles away resignedly.
13.modern-da: Melchisedec dukker op en forfærdelig kold aften, da Sara vender udmattet og sulten tilbage til kvisten, og hun har ingen smuler at give ham — hun har glemt det, fordi hun var for ulykkelig. Han sjakrer af sted resigneret.

14.modern-en: Melchisedec hides in his hole in terror when Ram Dass and the secretary enter the attic, peering at them through the crack. He does not understand their whispered conversation but is greatly relieved when they leave — and hopeful that they may have dropped crumbs.
14.modern-da: Melchisedec gemmer sig i sit hul i rædsel, da Ram Dass og sekretæren træder ind på kvisten, og kigger til dem gennem sprækken. Han forstår ikke deres hvidskede samtale, men er meget lettet, da de går — og håbefuld om, at de måske har tabt smuler.

15.modern-en: When Sara returns late from the kitchen after missing supper and finds Ermengarde in the attic, Melchisedec appears expectantly for his evening meal — but Sara has nothing to give him and apologizes. He shuffles away.
15.modern-da: Da Sara vender sent tilbage fra køkkenet efter at have mistet aftensmad og finder Ermengarde på kvisten, dukker Melchisedec forventningsfuldt op til sit aftensmåltid — men Sara har intet at give ham og undskylder. Han sjakrer af sted.

19.modern-en: Melchisedec is remembered fondly by Sara when she tells the story of the attic to the Large Family — part of the wonder of the skylight and the sparrows and the strange companionship of the garret life.
19.modern-da: Melchisedec huskes med kærlighed af Sara, da hun fortæller historien om kvisten til Den Store Familie — en del af undringen ved tagvinduet og spurvene og det mærkelige selskab fra kvisttilværelsen.

epithet.en: The doll who is meant to listen

1.modern-en: Sara and her father search many toy shops until Sara suddenly spots Emily in a window: "She is actually waiting there for us!" Emily is chosen because she looks as if she listens — and Sara needs a friend who will hear her talk about papa when he is gone. Emily is measured for a wardrobe as grand as Sara's own.
1.modern-da: Sara og hendes far gennemstrejfer mange legetøjsbutikker, til Sara pludselig spotter Emily i et vindue: »Hun venter faktisk der på os!« Emily vælges, fordi hun ser ud som om hun lytter — og Sara har brug for en ven, der vil høre hende tale om far, når han er borte. Emily måles op til en garderobe lige så pragtfuld som Saras.

2.modern-en: Sara leaves Emily with a book when she goes downstairs, telling Mariette she believes dolls read and walk when no one is looking — they only pretend to be still when people are present. Emily sits "reading" in her chair.
2.modern-da: Sara efterlader Emily med en bog, da hun går ned, og fortæller Mariette, at hun tror, at dukker læser og går rundt, når ingen kigger — de lader blot som om, de sidder stille, når folk er til stede. Emily sidder »læsende« i sin stol.

3.modern-en: Sara introduces Emily to Ermengarde and pretends that she was caught rushing back to her chair "like lightning" when the door opened. Ermengarde is allowed to hold Emily and is deeply impressed.
3.modern-da: Sara præsenterer Emily for Ermengarde og lader som om, at hun blev fanget i at løbe tilbage til sin stol »som et lyn«, da døren åbnede. Ermengarde får lov at holde Emily og er dybt imponeret.

5.modern-en: Emily sits in her own chair in Sara's sitting room, described as presiding like "a goddess" — part of what makes the room feel wonderful to Becky when she sneaks in to rest.
5.modern-da: Emily sidder i sin egen stol i Saras dagligstue, beskrevet som presiderende som »en gudinde« — en del af det, der får rummet til at føles vidunderligt for Becky, når hun lister ind for at hvile.

7.modern-en: When Sara is told her father is dead, she runs to her room and cries to Emily: "Do you hear? Papa is dead!" When Miss Minchin later orders her to put the doll down, Sara refuses: "No. She is all I have. My papa gave her to me." She takes Emily to the attic wrapped in black material.
7.modern-da: Da Sara får at vide, at hendes far er død, løber hun til sit værelse og råber til Emily: »Hører du? Far er død!« Da Miss Minchin senere beordrer hende til at sætte dukken ned, nægter Sara: »Nej. Det er alt, hvad jeg har. Min far gav hende til mig.« Hun tager Emily med til kvisten pakket i sort materiale.

8.modern-en: Emily sits in the attic with her fixed stare, which Sara begins to find eerie. Sara tries to believe Emily is a "good witch" who protects her, and has long conversations with her — or rather, one-sided monologues, since Emily never answers. The relationship between them becomes a measure of Sara's loneliness.
8.modern-da: Emily sidder på kvisten med sit faste blik, som Sara begynder at finde uhyggeligt. Sara forsøger at tro, at Emily er en »god heks«, der beskytter hende, og har lange samtaler med hende — eller rettere ensidige monologer, da Emily aldrig svarer. Forholdet imellem dem bliver et mål for Saras ensomhed.

10.modern-en: On one particularly awful night, Sara comes home cold and starving and knocks Emily off her chair in a burst of weeping: "You are nothing but a doll! You care for nothing. You are stuffed with sawdust. You never had a heart." Then she picks Emily up, apologizes, and kisses her.
10.modern-da: På en særlig forfærdelig aften vender Sara hjem kold og udsultet og slår Emily af stolen i et udbrud af gråd: »Du er bare en dukke! Du bryder dig om ingenting. Du er fyldt med savsmuld. Du har aldrig haft et hjerte.« Derefter samler hun Emily op, undskylder og kysser hende.

15.modern-en: When Miss Minchin breaks up the party and the dream collapses, Sara picks Emily up in the emptied attic and says: "There isn't any banquet left, Emily. And there isn't any princess. There is nothing left but the prisoners in the Bastille."
15.modern-da: Da Miss Minchin opbryder festen og drømmen bryder sammen, samler Sara Emily op i den tømte kvist og siger: »Der er ikke mere banket, Emily. Og der er ingen prinsesse. Der er ingenting tilbage undtagen fangerne i Bastillen.«
